files.purpose: The Metal stitchable distortion shader that reproduces the macOS Dock genie effect for archived rows: it maps each destination pixel back into the flying row's frame through a fixed funnel whose sides bend from the row's width down to a narrow neck at the target point.
key_symbols: [[ stitchable ]] float2 genie(float2 position, float progress, float4 source, float2 target)
locals: t, pinch, slide, width, height, flip, x0, y0, targetY, positionY, travel, depth, bend, neck, left, right, u, sourceY
calls_into: Invoked from Swift as ShaderLibrary.genie(.float(progress), .float4(x, y, w, h), .float2(target.x, target.y)) in Genie.swift
platform_assumptions: Metal Shading Language compiled into the app's default shader library
SwiftUI's [[stitchable]] distortionEffect convention: the function receives a destination position and returns the source position to sample
feature_notes: progress is animation progress 0...1, explicitly never a clock; source is the row's frame (x, y, width, height) and target the neck, both in the layer's coordinates
pinch = smoothstep(0.0, 0.45, t) controls how far the sides have bent in; slide = smoothstep(0.2, 1.0, t) controls how far the row has travelled
flip = 1.0 when target.y >= source.y + height * 0.5, else -1.0; the vertical axis is mirrored on the way in and out so a target above the row funnels upwards
travel = max(targetY - y0, height); depth = clamp((positionY - y0) / travel, 0, 1); bend = pinch * smoothstep(0.0, 1.0, depth)
neck = min(24.0, width): the funnel's narrow end is at most 24 points wide
left = mix(x0, target.x - neck * 0.5, bend), right = mix(x0 + width, target.x + neck * 0.5, bend), u = (position.x - left) / max(right - left, 0.0001)

Three discard conditions return 'nothing' (-100000, -100000), sampling nothing: positionY > targetY (past the neck), u outside [0, 1] (outside the funnel), and sourceY outside [y0, y0 + height] (past the row)
sourceY = positionY - slide * (targetY - y0); the returned sample is float2(x0 + u * width, flip * sourceY)
unresolved_questions: Whether the shader file is compiled into the default library automatically by the Xcode target (no build settings are visible from this file), though Genie.swift's use of ShaderLibrary.genie implies it is

Flight opacity: 1 until progress > 0.9, then max(0, (1 - progress) / 0.1) - a fade over the last 10% of the animation

maxSampleOffset (reach) = CGSize(width: abs(target.x - frame.midX) + frame.width, height: abs(target.y - frame.midY) + frame.height), so the offscreen pass is padded by that instead of the whole window

The flight view removes itself after GenieAnimator.duration - 0.03 seconds, just before the keyframes finish, so it never springs back

files.purpose: The working indicators ported from Zeron: the opacity wave maths and accent-derived row tints, the 3x3 WorkingSpinner shown while a reply is written, the 2x3 MiniSpinner that snakes clockwise for working threads in lists (with a still, image-renderable variant), the layer-backed NSView that plays the pulse on the render server, and the rotating WorkingWords vocabulary seeded per thread.
key_symbols: struct MiniSpinner (cellSize default 2.4, isStill default false) + MiniSpinner.ring + MiniSpinner.cells
state_owned: SpinnerLayerView: cells, columns, cellSize, animated, theme: AppTheme?, cellLayers: [CALayer]
Static tables: WorkingSpinner.cells (9 cells), MiniSpinner.ring (6 positions), MiniSpinner.cells (6 cells), WorkingWords.words (22 words)
side_effects: Observes ThemeManager.didChange in init and removes the observer in deinit
Adds a repeating CAKeyframeAnimation per cell layer to the render server (isRemovedOnCompletion = false)
Re-resolves the dynamic system accent on viewDidChangeEffectiveAppearance and viewDidMoveToWindow
platform_assumptions: AppKit bottom-left layer coordinates: placeCells explicitly flips row order (rows - 1 - cell.row) so row 0 draws at the top
NSViewRepresentable hosting, and the note that ImageRenderer cannot capture AppKit views, which is why MiniSpinner(isStill: true) exists for the archive ghost
Dynamic macOS system accent colour resolved inside effectiveAppearance.performAsCurrentDrawingAppearance

ui_elements: WorkingSpinner: 3x3 grid, default cellSize 3.5, cell gap = cellSize * 0.8
MiniSpinner: 2 columns x 3 rows, default cellSize 2.4, accessibilityLabel Text("Working")
Row tints: accent blended 0.38 toward white (top row), the accent itself (middle), accent blended 0.22 toward black (bottom)
StillSpinnerCells: VStack/HStack of Rectangles at spacing cellSize * 0.8, each at GradientSpin.opacity(phase: -lag)
contentSize = (columns * cellSize + (columns - 1) * gap) x (rows * cellSize + (rows - 1) * gap); the grid is centred in the frame SwiftUI hands out with rounded origins
feature_notes: Opacity curve: full at phase 0, eases down to dim 0.1 by 45% via smoothstep (1 - 0.9 * t*t*(3-2t)), holds dim until 92%, then rises linearly back to full by 100%; the phase wraps and negative phases are normalised
Pulse period 0.75s, sampled at 41 points (sampleCount 40) into a linear CAKeyframeAnimation per cell, repeating forever
WorkingSpinner lag = sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy) / 2.5 where dx = column - 1 and dy = 2 - row, i.e. distance from bottom-centre, so the wave travels upward
MiniSpinner lag = ring index / 6 over the clockwise perimeter order (0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (2,1), (2,0), (1,0)
Every animation starts at layer.convertTime(1, from: nil), so every spinner in the app pulses in step
Reduce motion (accessibilityReduceMotion) turns animated off, and each layer is frozen at GradientSpin.opacity(phase: -cell.lag)
The layers replaced a Canvas on a 30 Hz TimelineView that woke SwiftUI thirty times a second on the main thread for the whole length of a turn

configure() early-outs unless the layer count changed, the theme changed, or columns/cellSize/animated changed; a theme change retints via the ThemeManager.didChange notification because a row that never re-renders would keep the old colours

WorkingWords rotates every 7 seconds (rotateSeconds: Int64 = 7) through 22 words: Thinking, Pondering, Scheming, Brewing, Weaving, Tinkering, Musing, Composing, Sifting, Untangling, Distilling, Sketching, Plotting, Riffing, Combobulating, Percolating, Marinating, Noodling, Puzzling, Conjuring, Creating, Dancing

The word index is (FNV-1a seed of the thread identifier &+ elapsedSeconds / 7) % 22, with FNV-1a offset basis 0xcbf29ce484222325 and prime 0x100000001b3, so two threads working at once say different things
